linux-headers: add nl80211_sta_info enums Kernel support for following nl80211_sta_info enums is necessary for user-space to populate their respective entries 1. NL80211_STA_INFO_ACK_SIGNAL - support to get ack signal in probe client response and in station info from user 2. NL80211_STA_INFO_ACK_SIGNAL_AVG - avg signal strength of ACK frames 3. NL80211_STA_INFO_RX_MPDUS - total number of received packets 4. NL80211_STA_INFO_FCS_ERROR_COUNT - total number of packets (MPDUs) received with an FCS error 5. NL80211_STA_INFO_CONNECTED_TO_GATE - gate connectivity in station info 6. NL80211_STA_INFO_TX_DURATION - aggregate PPDU duration for all frames sent to the station 7. NL80211_STA_INFO_AIRTIME_WEIGHT - current airtime weight for station 8. NL80211_STA_INFO_AIRTIME_LINK_METRIC - airtime link metric for mesh station BUG=b:122467941 TEST=Build for Jetstream products Change-Id: Ifcea902d8358585d966095f07526a6f8b6b816d8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1544980 Tested-by: NARAYANRADDI MASTI <nmasti@google.com> Tested-by: Omkar Bahirat <omkarvijay@google.com> Commit-Ready: NARAYANRADDI MASTI <nmasti@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

runtime_probe: separate the evaluation to different processes We separate the Eval() implementation into different stages so they can be done in more than one process, which leads to a better security management model. Previously, we tied everything in a single process, where the sandbox is an union of all possible probe functions. It is not obvious on what exactly the seccomp / capabilities / minijail arguments designated to a probe function if we scale the number of probe functions. An illustrated example is from init runtime_probe [1] Eval() for probe funtion A [1] Eval() for probe funtion B [1] to init runtime_probe [2] Eval() for probe function A [2] evaluation under sandbox [2] InvokeHelper() [2] // TODO: fold into debugd in next CL runtime_probe_helper (for probe function A) [3] EvalInHelper() [3] evaluation under sandbox [2] Eval() for probe function B [2] evaluation under sandbox [2] InvokeHelper() [2] // TODO: fold into debugd in next CL runtime_probe_helper (for probe function B) [4] EvalInHelper() [4] evaluation under sandbox [2] , where the sandbox surfaces are: [1]: union of [2], [3], [4] [2]: communicate to others, for example: mojo, D-Bus [3]: extended sandbox just for probe function A [4]: extended sandbox just for probe function B With this change, we can apply smaller sandboxes instead of a giant sandbox in the future. BUG=b:129313193 TEST=USE="cros-debug" emerge-nami runtime_probe cros_deploy $ACTIVE_DUT runtime_probe runtime_probe --debug Cq-Depend: chromium:1545471 Change-Id: Ie25729653012421579eca980fc84d880688a8974 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1545594 Tested-by: Clark Chung <ckclark@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Clark Chung <ckclark@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jorge Lucangeli Obes <jorgelo@chromium.org>

CRAS: Remove frames from input devices when missing callback The stream may miss callback due to audio thread wake up late. For that situation, we will reset stream's schedule to fix it. However, it also makes some frames remain in the device permanently. To avoid increasing delay, we can keep the hw_level less than 2 * largest_cb_level. When it exceeds, adjust the number of frames to earliest min_cb_ts of all input devices by dropping frames. BUG=chromium:918462 TEST=The hardware level doesn't increase when missing callback. (Test on Panther) Change-Id: Ie1d9020bddb57c0a2d14a1b1eeb22d3bd4449749 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1673766 Tested-by: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Yu-Hsuan Hsu <yuhsuan@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Cheng-Yi Chiang <cychiang@chromium.org>

mount_gpt_image.sh: fix unmounting when --from is not used When the image is omitted, FLAGS_from is empty, but we still try to construct paths based on it and then use them (including passing to losetup tools). We don't actually use those results when the file is omitted which is why we unmount fine. We also disable `set -e` in the unmount path so we can unmount as much as possible even if there are some errors which is why we don't see hard failures. We can improve that logic in a followup. BUG=chromium:955147 TEST=running mount & unmount no longer shows losetup errors ./mount_gpt_image.sh --from=../build/images/betty/latest/ --image=chromiumos_qemu_image.bin --safe ./mount_gpt_image.sh --unmount Change-Id: Ide995ac8943334371690b85364b9c8de0d4a997c Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1700156 Tested-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Achuith Bhandarkar <achuith@chromium.org>
